llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability that Israel strikes five different countries in 2026 is a diffuse signal of expected broadening Middle East military escalation. The most defensible liquid implications are a modest geopolitical risk premium in crude oil (USO up) and a slight bid in defense/aerospace equities (ITA up). Both mappings are weak and noisy because this is a full-year aggregate resolution rather than a dated imminent-strike event; neither is likely to clear the 700bps tradable bar in 12 hours. Treat as low-confidence research signals, not actionable trades.
key_assumptions: A probability jump reflects new expectations of regional escalation rather than noise or stale news
Escalation across multiple countries plausibly implicates oil-supply-relevant geographies (Iran, Gulf, Red Sea)
Oil and defense are the cleanest liquid proxies for Middle East conflict risk
failure_modes: The move reverses as a transient prediction-market blip with no real-world driver
The escalation news is already public and fully priced into oil/defense
Strikes are on non-oil-relevant countries (e.g. Syria, Lebanon, Yemen) with minimal supply impact, so crude barely reacts
Macro factors (Fed, growth data, inventories) dominate oil over the 12h window, swamping the geopolitical signal
ITA is driven by US budget cycles and has only tenuous exposure to a single foreign conflict probability
